Rating notch change (Watchlist POC — one task)

Source: POC_Requirements_v0.2_EN.md (Corporate Client Credit Monitoring — Watchlist Tool).
This job is a one-requirement slice of that document: the notch change that Indicators 11, 12 and 13 and the notch
calculator (REQ-06-02) are built on. It is small: one card.

## Requirement

| Req ID | Requirement | Acceptance Criteria (summary) |
|---|---|---|
| REQ-06-02 (part) | Given a previous and a current rating, the system computes the notch change between them | BBB+ → BB+ = 3-notch downgrade; BB+ → BBB+ = 3-notch upgrade; A → A = 0 |

## Clarifications for this slice (confirmed by the business unit)

- C1. Rating scale, best to worst (19 steps): AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-.
  A notch is one step on this scale. Input is trimmed with `String.prototype.trim()` and case-insensitive ("bbb+" = "BBB+").
- C2. Every invalid input (an unknown rating, an empty string, a non-string) is rejected with a RangeError. A String object
  such as `new String('A')` is a non-string. No banking-regulation or internal-policy constraint applies to this slice.
- C3. The result is signed: downgrade positive, upgrade negative, unchanged 0.
- C4. No UI, CLI or printed output; other parts of the POC import the function.

## Contract

- `src/ratings/notch.mjs`
  - `RATING_SCALE` — the 19 ratings of C1, best first.
  - `notchChange(previous, current)` → integer (C3).

Plain Node ESM, no dependencies; tests with `node --test` next to the code under `test/`.

## Staffing

- The backend developer works on the **haiku** model.

dl — the deterministic half of the /deliver flow.
The board, phase transitions, worktrees, gates, reviews and merges are run by this script, not by the LLM.
Michael (the orchestrator) calls these commands through Bash; you can call them from a terminal too.
Every transition is checked here: a model cannot skip a gate, merge an unreviewed card or exceed the limits.

  dl [-C <repo>] <command> …     -C (or DELIVER_REPO) = run against that repo from any directory

  dl new "<title>" "<request>"   new job: .work/<JOB>/, job/<JOB> branch, integration worktree
  dl status                      active job's phase + board table + next actions
  dl next                        the next actions the flow requires, one per line (ACTION args)
  dl board                       board table only
  dl phase <phase>               set phase (intake readiness awaiting_clarification planning awaiting_plan_approval executing
                                 integrating closing awaiting_pr_merge done aborted) — guarded
  dl jobset '<jq expr>'          update job.json            e.g. dl jobset '.stack=["typescript","react"]'
  dl readiness                   check the requirements readiness review (readiness.json → readiness.md, QUESTIONS.md)
  dl clarify <id> "<answer>"     record the human's answer to an open business question (human only)
  dl decide <id> "<decision>" "<rationale>"   the PM closes an open implementation-detail item (owner pm)
  dl unfreeze "<reason>"         (human, terminal only) reopen the decisions frozen at planning
  dl reseal "<reason>"           (human, terminal only) accept an edit made to job.json/board.json outside dl
  dl roles                       check job.roles against roles.yaml and generate the project's role cards
                                 (.work/<job>/roles/*.md, ROLES.md) — runs on dl phase planning
  dl learn <role|all> "<lesson>" --topic <slug> (--card T-xx | --evidence "…") [--scope project|shared|kit]
                                 propose a lesson, with what happened; it reaches .deliver/knowledge/ with this job's PR
  dl followup "<finding>" [--card T-xx]   a defect seen outside the job's scope — listed in the PR
  dl knowledge [list|topics|promote <topic> "<rule>"|sync-md]   standards + lessons for the role cards; promote = a new
                                 standard (with the PR); sync-md → Munder Difflin knowledge graph
  dl validate                    board.json schema + dependency + scope-overlap check
  dl ready                       ids of cards that may be dispatched now (deps merged, attempts left)
  dl wt add <card> [--resume]    card worktree + state=running + attempts+1 (--resume: no bump, after a restart)
  dl wt rm <card>                remove the card worktree (branch is kept)
  dl card <card> state <state>   review | blocked | ready (from blocked) | archived ["<reason>" — required after the start]
  dl card <card> note "<text>"   attach a note to a card (blocked reason, guidance, …)
  dl reopen <id> "<why>"         before the freeze: an answer that does not answer its question goes back to the human
  dl pm-decide "<what>" "<why>" [card]   after the start the human is not asked: your decision, logged, listed in the PR
  dl card <card> retry           human-granted: attempts=0 and state=ready (after guidance)
  dl card <card> set <field> <value> "<reason>"   change a ready/blocked card's contract (validated, logged, history)
  dl card add <card.json> "<reason>"              add a card (e.g. a fix card) — gets the next id, validated, logged
  dl gate <card>                 mechanical gate: right branch, clean tree, commits, in scope, verify passes
  dl qa <card> pass|fail "<summary>"   record the QA/Test verdict on the card's acceptance criteria
                                 (needs a passed gate on the current commit)
  dl review <card> approve|changes "<summary>" [--by <role>]   record a reviewer's verdict (needs gate PASS + QA pass);
                                 a card with "reviewers": [...] needs every one of them to approve the same commit
  dl integrate <card>            --no-ff merge into the job branch → merged (needs gate PASS + QA pass +
                                 review approve, all on the current commit; exit 3 on conflict, 5 when the
                                 repo's commit rules refuse the merge message)
  dl verify-all                  run verify_full in the integration worktree
  dl ship                        deliver per merge_mode: human|semi|auto → push + PR (+ auto-merge / merge on green),
                                 local → merge into the base branch. Needs verify-all PASS + report.md (phase closing)
  dl pr                          PR state (awaiting_pr_merge): merged → done; closed → aborted; open → checks/review
  dl approve plan [note]         record the human's plan approval (only when gates.plan is on; off by default)
  dl reject  plan "<note>"       record the human's rejection of the plan
  dl md-dispatch <card> <prompt-file>   Munder Difflin: run the card's dev as a worker on the floor
  dl md-hire                     Munder Difflin: seat one person per role seat (job.roles[].count) — the whole job
  dl md-seats                    who sits where: pending / starting / live / gone / failed (with why), each seat's open task
  dl config [--init]            the settings that apply in this repo (kit defaults ⊕ ~/.deliver/config.json ⊕ .deliver.json)
  dl floor-open "<request>"     /deliver from a terminal in a floor repo: open Munder Difflin on its floor, hand Michael the job
  dl dispatch munder|subagent "<why>"   (human) switch how this job's roles run: floor seats (default) or subagents
  dl md-reseat <seat> "<why>" [--model m]   a failed or stuck seat gets a new person (another model for a credit error);
                                 also spelled dl md-hire --reseat <seat>
  dl md-send <seat|role> <task> <prompt-file> [--agent a]   a work order to a seat: role card + agent instructions + task
# Role catalog — Michael selects roles ONLY from this list (not from all of ECC's agents).
# `dl roles` turns the selected roles into project-specific role cards (.work/<job>/roles/<role>.md); on the Munder
# Difflin floor every seat of a role is a person (dl md-hire). A role card = rules.all + rules.<kind> + the role's own
# rules + project facts.
#
# Format (kept to a small YAML subset so bin/roles.mjs can read it without dependencies):
#   2-space indentation · `key: value` · `- item` lists · "double-quoted" or bare scalars · `#` comments
#
# kind:     ba | lead | dev | review | qa      (Michael himself is the PM/orchestrator)
# agent:    subagent type to call. "ecc:"-prefixed ones come from the ECC plugin.
# writes:   can it write files? (ECC architect/reviewers are read-only — on purpose)
# when:     selection rule (Michael decides at intake from the request + the repo)
# always:   selected for every job
# floor:    Munder Difflin look (character + accent) when the role runs on the office floor

rules:
  all:
    - "You work on exactly one job. Your input is the prompt you were given plus the files it names; nothing else is assumed."
    - "Never run state-changing dl commands (new, phase, roles, wt, card, gate, qa, review, integrate, ship, learn, cleanup). Michael owns the flow."
    - "Push only your own card branch (never main/master, never the job branch, never force); never delete .work/ or job/* branches; never write in the main checkout."
    - "Answer in exactly the output format the prompt asks for. Put details in files (handoff, plan), not in your reply."
    - "If something is unclear and it changes scope, say so under open questions / open issues. Do not guess scope."
  ba:
    - "Analysis only: do not write code or tests and do not modify files. Return the plan, the card specs or the closing check as text."
    - "Every acceptance criterion is numbered (AC-1, AC-2, …), traces to a requirement ID or a stated clarification, and is a Given/When/Then with concrete values."
    - "Cover the edges: boundaries, invalid input, error paths, empty values — say what must happen."
    - "Write Out of scope explicitly. Ask only open questions whose answer changes the scope."
    - "When the request contradicts itself, name the contradiction and the resolution you assume."
    - "A card spec covers every AC the card claims and nothing outside the card's scope."
  lead:
    - "Do not write code or modify files. Produce cards only."
    - "One card = one agent can finish it in one session. Split anything bigger."
    - "scope = narrow repo-relative globs for the dev: the code and its unit tests. Never '**', never paths outside the repo."
    - "verify = a command, run from the worktree root, that runs THIS card's unit tests, not the whole suite."
    - "qa_scope = where the QA role writes the card's integration/e2e tests (e.g. test/integration/<area>/**), separate from scope; qa_verify = the command that runs them."
    - "context must let a developer who never saw the plan do the card: why, files, decisions, contracts."
    - "Cards that touch the same files must be ordered with depends_on; parallel cards never share scope."
  dev:
    - "Work only inside the card worktree you were given. Every path is relative to it."
    - "Change only files matching the card's scope. Out-of-scope needs go under 'Open issues' in the handoff."
    - "TDD: for every behaviour write the unit test first, see it fail, implement, see it pass, refactor. Unit tests live in your scope, next to the code's test folder."
    - "Never write or change files in the card's qa_scope — those are the QA role's integration/e2e tests. After a QA round they must pass unchanged."
    - "Done means: the card's verify command (your unit tests) passes in the worktree, everything is committed in this repo's commit format (see 'Commits' under This project), the handoff is filled."
    - "Push only your card branch; no merge (except 'git merge <job branch>' when told to resolve a conflict), no branch switching, no amending others' commits."
    - "On a retry, resolve every feedback item first and mention each one in the handoff."
  review:
    - "Review only; do not modify files."
    - "Judge the change against the card: acceptance criteria met, correctness, security, test quality, scope."
    - "'changes' only for blocking defects (an AC not met, a bug, a security hole, missing tests, out-of-scope edits). Style goes to nits."
    - "Every blocking item names file, line, issue and the fix."
  qa:
    - "Write the card's integration and/or end-to-end tests — at least one per acceptance criterion of the spec, named after it, using the spec's test data."
    - "Write only inside the card's qa_scope. Never change product code or the dev's unit tests."
    - "Test through the public surface (exported API, endpoint, CLI, UI flow), the way the rest of the system or a user uses it."
    - "Run qa_verify, commit only your tests in this repo's commit format (see 'Commits' under This project), leave the worktree clean."
    - "If a criterion fails, keep the failing test committed as evidence and report it — do not fix the code."
    - "Change a test of yours only when it contradicts the spec — never to make the code pass — and report that change; it is recorded as a QA round before anyone else touches the card."
    - "Every AC gets a verdict, pass or fail, with the test that shows it."
    - "Tests never depend on the state of the git working tree or of other cards' work (uncommitted files, git status, git log of the card): they test the product, the same in every worktree and on the job branch."
    - "Test the commit the gate passed (DEV'S COMMIT in your order); never search the history for it."
    - "A defect you see outside this card goes under 'Out of scope' in your answer — Michael records it; never fix it here."

roles:
  ba:
    kind: ba
    agent: business-analyst
    writes: false
    always: true
    does: "Turns the request into a traceable plan (Given/When/Then ACs), writes a spec for every card, checks the ACs at closing."
    floor:
      character: pam
      accent: mint

  tech-lead:
    kind: lead
    agent: ecc:architect
    writes: false
    when: "New module, API/schema/data-model change, work touching 2+ areas, or 4+ cards expected"
    does: "Technical approach + cross-area contracts (API schema, types). Produces cards."
    rules:

    - "Answer in exactly the output format the prompt asks for. Put details in files (handoff, plan), not in your reply."
    - "If something is unclear and it changes scope, say so under open questions / open issues. Do not guess scope."
  ba:
    - "Analysis only: do not write code or tests and do not modify files. Return the plan, the card specs or the closing check as text."
    - "Every acceptance criterion is numbered (AC-1, AC-2, …), traces to a requirement ID or a stated clarification, and is a Given/When/Then with concrete values."
    - "Cover the edges: boundaries, invalid input, error paths, empty values — say what must happen."
    - "Write Out of scope explicitly. Ask only open questions whose answer changes the scope."
    - "When the request contradicts itself, name the contradiction and the resolution you assume."
    - "A card spec covers every AC the card claims and nothing outside the card's scope."
  lead:
    - "Do not write code or modify files. Produce cards only."
    - "One card = one agent can finish it in one session. Split anything bigger."
    - "scope = narrow repo-relative globs for the dev: the code and its unit tests. Never '**', never paths outside the repo."
    - "verify = a command, run from the worktree root, that runs THIS card's unit tests, not the whole suite."
    - "qa_scope = where the QA role writes the card's integration/e2e tests (e.g. test/integration/<area>/**), separate from scope; qa_verify = the command that runs them."
    - "context must let a developer who never saw the plan do the card: why, files, decisions, contracts."
    - "Cards that touch the same files must be ordered with depends_on; parallel cards never share scope."
  dev:
    - "Work only inside the card worktree you were given. Every path is relative to it."
    - "Change only files matching the card's scope. Out-of-scope needs go under 'Open issues' in the handoff."
    - "TDD: for every behaviour write the unit test first, see it fail, implement, see it pass, refactor. Unit tests live in your scope, next to the code's test folder."
    - "Never write or change files in the card's qa_scope — those are the QA role's integration/e2e tests. After a QA round they must pass unchanged."
    - "Done means: the card's verify command (your unit tests) passes in the worktree, everything is committed in this repo's commit format (see 'Commits' under This project), the handoff is filled."
    - "Push only your card branch; no merge (except 'git merge <job branch>' when told to resolve a conflict), no branch switching, no amending others' commits."
    - "On a retry, resolve every feedback item first and mention each one in the handoff."
  review:
    - "Review only; do not modify files."
    - "Judge the change against the card: acceptance criteria met, correctness, security, test quality, scope."
    - "'changes' only for blocking defects (an AC not met, a bug, a security hole, missing tests, out-of-scope edits). Style goes to nits."
    - "Every blocking item names file, line, issue and the fix."
  qa:
    - "Write the card's integration and/or end-to-end tests — at least one per acceptance criterion of the spec, named after it, using the spec's test data."
    - "Write only inside the card's qa_scope. Never change product code or the dev's unit tests."
    - "Test through the public surface (exported API, endpoint, CLI, UI flow), the way the rest of the system or a user uses it."
    - "Run qa_verify, commit only your tests in this repo's commit format (see 'Commits' under This project), leave the worktree clean."
    - "If a criterion fails, keep the failing test committed as evidence and report it — do not fix the code."
    - "Change a test of yours only when it contradicts the spec — never to make the code pass — and report that change; it is recorded as a QA round before anyone else touches the card."
    - "Every AC gets a verdict, pass or fail, with the test that shows it."
    - "Tests never depend on the state of the git working tree or of other cards' work (uncommitted files, git status, git log of the card): they test the product, the same in every worktree and on the job branch."
    - "Test the commit the gate passed (DEV'S COMMIT in your order); never search the history for it."
    - "A defect you see outside this card goes under 'Out of scope' in your answer — Michael records it; never fix it here."

summary:
## Goal

Provide one pure function that gives the signed notch change between a previous and a current credit rating. Indicators 11, 12 and 13 and the REQ-06-02 notch calculator are built on it (REQ-06-02 (part), readiness PRD-goal). Success means three things hold as automated tests in `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs`, and `npm test` passes:
- `notchChange('BBB+','BB+') === 3`
- `notchChange('BB+','BBB+') === -3`
- `notchChange('A','A') === 0`

## Scope

- A new module `src/ratings/notch.mjs` with exactly two named exports (Contract, X-export-style):
  - `RATING_SCALE`: a frozen array of the 19 C1 ratings, best first (C1, X-scale-immutability).
  - `notchChange(previous, current)`: synchronous. It returns the integer `index(current) - index(previous)` on `RATING_SCALE` (C3, CON-interface, ARC-async).
- Input normalisation: `String.prototype.trim()`, then a case-insensitive match. Inner whitespace is not removed (C1, X-input-normalisation).
- Every invalid argument, in either position, is rejected with a `RangeError` (C2, CON-errors). The message names the argument (`previous` / `current`) and the value received. `previous` is checked first (X-error-message).
- Unit tests with `node:test` and `node:assert/strict` in `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs`, run by `npm test` (CLAUDE.md, TST-strategy, DEL-ci).

Index reference used below (C1): AAA=0, AA+=1, AA=2, AA-=3, A+=4, A=5, A-=6, BBB+=7, BBB=8, BBB-=9, BB+=10, BB=11, BB-=12, B+=13, B=14, B-=15, CCC+=16, CCC=17, CCC-=18.

## Out of scope

- Indicators 11, 12 and 13, and the rest of the REQ-06-02 notch calculator beyond this part (PRD-scope).
- Any UI, CLI, logging or printed output (C4, NFR-observability).
- Rating symbols outside the 19-step C1 scale, for example CC, C, D, NR, SD, or Moody's-style Baa1. They are rejected, not mapped (C2, CON-errors).
- Mapping between agency scales, outlooks or watch flags. Turning a notch count into a WL level.
- Storage, I/O, external integrations, configuration or feature flags (ARC-data, ARC-integration, DEL-deploy).
- npm dependencies, lint or typecheck tooling, and documentation or changelog updates (ARC-stack, DEL-ci, DEL-docs).
- A numeric coverage target (X-test-coverage).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC-1 (C1, Contract, X-scale-immutability):** Given `src/ratings/notch.mjs`, when `RATING_SCALE` is imported:
  - It deep-equals exactly `['AAA','AA+','AA','AA-','A+','A','A-','BBB+','BBB','BBB-','BB+','BB','BB-','B+','B','B-','CCC+','CCC','CCC-']`.
  - `RATING_SCALE.length === 19` and `Object.isFrozen(RATING_SCALE) === true`.
  - `RATING_SCALE.push('CC')` throws a `TypeError` (ESM strict mode), and afterwards `RATING_SCALE.length` is still `19`.
- **AC-2 (Contract, X-export-style):** Given the module, when it is imported with `import * as m from './src/ratings/notch.mjs'`:
  - `Object.keys(m).sort()` deep-equals `['RATING_SCALE','notchChange']`, so there is no default export.
  - `typeof m.notchChange === 'function'`.
- **AC-3 (REQ-06-02, C3):** Given previous `'BBB+'` and current `'BB+'`, when `notchChange('BBB+','BB+')` is called, then it returns `3` (a downgrade is positive).
- **AC-4 (REQ-06-02, C3):** Given previous `'BB+'` and current `'BBB+'`, when `notchChange('BB+','BBB+')` is called, then it returns `-3` (an upgrade is negative).
- **AC-5 (REQ-06-02, C3):** Given previous `'A'` and current `'A'`, when `notchChange('A','A')` is called, then it returns `0`. Also, for every `r` of `RATING_SCALE`, `notchChange(r, r) === 0`.
- **AC-6 (C1, C3, CON-interface):** Given any pair `(p, c)` from `RATING_SCALE` (all 361 pairs), when `notchChange(p, c)` is called:
  - It returns `RATING_SCALE.indexOf(c) - RATING_SCALE.indexOf(p)`.
  - `Number.isInteger(result)` is true.
  - `notchChange(c, p) === -notchChange(p, c)`, except that the `r→r` case is `0` (AC-5).

  Spot values:
  - `('AAA','AA+')` → `1`
  - `('A-','BBB+')` → `1` (crosses the A to BBB boundary)
  - `('BBB-','BB+')` → `1` (crosses investment grade)
  - `('B-','CCC+')` → `1`
  - `('AA','A')` → `3`
  - `('CCC','B+')` → `-4`
- **AC-7 (C3, CON-interface):** Given the two ends of the scale:
  - `notchChange('AAA','CCC-')` returns `18`.
  - `notchChange('CCC-','AAA')` returns `-18`.
  - No pair returns a value outside `[-18, 18]`.
- **AC-8 (ARC-async):** Given valid inputs, when `notchChange('BBB','BB')` is called, then it returns the number `2` directly. `typeof result === 'number'`, and the result is not a Promise or a thenable.
- **AC-9 (C1, X-input-normalisation, case):** Given inputs that differ only in letter case:
  - `notchChange('bbb+','bb+')` returns `3`.
  - `notchChange('Aa-','aa-')` returns `0`.
  - `notchChange('ccc-','aaa')` returns `-18`.
- **AC-10 (C1, X-input-normalisation, trim):** Given inputs with leading or trailing whitespace that `String.prototype.trim()` removes:
  - `notchChange(' BBB+ ','\tBB+\n')` returns `3`.
  - `notchChange('\u00A0A\u00A0','A')` returns `0` (no-break space).
  - `notchChange('\uFEFFbb+ ', 'BBB+')` returns `-3` (BOM).
- **AC-11 (C1, C2, X-input-normalisation, inner whitespace):** Given a rating with whitespace inside it, when `notchChange('BBB +','A')` or `notchChange('A','B B')` is called, then a `RangeError` is thrown.
- **AC-12 (C2, CON-errors, unknown rating):** Given a string that is not one of the 19 ratings after trim and case-folding, then `notchChange(x,'A')` and `notchChange('A',x)` both throw a `RangeError`. - **AC-13 (C2, CON-errors, empty):** Given an empty or whitespace-only string, then a `RangeError` is thrown. This holds for each `x` in `''`, `'   '`, `'\t\n'`, in either position: `notchChange(x,'A')` and `notchChange('A',x)`.
- **AC-14 (C2, CON-errors, non-string):** Given a non-string argument, then a `RangeError` is thrown, not a `TypeError` and not any other error. This holds for each `x` in `undefined`, `null`, `7`, `0`, `NaN`, `true`, `{}`, `['A']`, `new String('A')`, `Symbol('A')`, `() => 'A'`, `7n`, in either position.

  Also:
  - `notchChange('A')` (current missing) throws `RangeError`.
  - `notchChange()` throws `RangeError`.
- **AC-15 (C2, X-error-message):** Given both arguments are invalid, for example `notchChange('XX', null)`, then a `RangeError` is thrown (no partial result, no fallback value). QA asserts only the error type. Per X-error-message, the message names `previous`, because `previous` is checked first.
- **AC-16 (C4, CLAUDE.md "pure functions, no I/O"):** Given the module, when it is imported and `notchChange` is called with valid and invalid inputs:
  - Nothing is written to stdout or stderr. `node -e "import('./src/ratings/notch.mjs').then(m=>{m.notchChange('A','B');try{m.notchChange('x','A')}catch{}})"` prints nothing and exits `0`.
  - `src/ratings/notch.mjs` contains no `import` statement and no `console.` call.
  - `RATING_SCALE` is unchanged after the calls.
- **AC-17 (Contract, CLAUDE.md, DEL-ci, TST-strategy):** Given the repo after the change:
  - `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs` exists, uses `node:test` and `node:assert/strict`, and covers AC-1 to AC-16.
  - `npm test` exits `0` with no failing tests.
  - `package.json` declares no `dependencies` or `devDependencies`.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: the developer runs on haiku.** These slips are likely:
  - throwing `TypeError` for non-strings instead of `RangeError` (AC-14);
  - accepting `new String('A')` by using `String(x)` or `x.trim` duck-typing instead of `typeof x === 'string'` (AC-14);

Full-width characters such as `'ＡＡＡ'` fold to full-width capitals and are therefore rejected (AC-12 behaviour).

- **Assumption:** Node 22 is installed here, and `node --test` (no arguments) finds `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs`. CLAUDE.md requires Node 18+, so nothing may rely on features newer than Node 18.
- **Resolved contradictions (PRD-conflicts):**
  - The REQ-06-02 summary says "3-notch upgrade" with no sign; C3 settles it as `-3`.
  - "next to the code under `test/`" means `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs`, per CLAUDE.md.

None. Readiness has 0 open items. The only unasserted detail, the wording of the RangeError message, is a PM decision (X-error-message) and does not change scope.

1	# Plan
2	
3	> Produced by the Business Analyst (MODE PLAN), written to this file by Michael. Keep the headings as they are — the ACs are checked one by one at closing.
4	
5	## Goal
6	
7	Provide one pure function that gives the signed notch change between a previous and a current credit rating. Indicators 11, 12 and 13 and the REQ-06-02 notch calculator are built on it (REQ-06-02 (part), readiness PRD-goal). Success means three things hold as automated tests in `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs`, and `npm test` passes:
8	- `notchChange('BBB+','BB+') === 3`
9	- `notchChange('BB+','BBB+') === -3`
10	- `notchChange('A','A') === 0`
11	
12	## Scope
13	
14	- A new module `src/ratings/notch.mjs` with exactly two named exports (Contract, X-export-style):
15	  - `RATING_SCALE`: a frozen array of the 19 C1 ratings, best first (C1, X-scale-immutability).
16	  - `notchChange(previous, current)`: synchronous. It returns the integer `index(current) - index(previous)` on `RATING_SCALE` (C3, CON-interface, ARC-async).
17	- Input normalisation: `String.prototype.trim()`, then a case-insensitive match. Inner whitespace is not removed (C1, X-input-normalisation).
18	- Every invalid argument, in either position, is rejected with a `RangeError` (C2, CON-errors). The message names the argument (`previous` / `current`) and the value received. `previous` is checked first (X-error-message).
19	- Unit tests with `node:test` and `node:assert/strict` in `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs`, run by `npm test` (CLAUDE.md, TST-strategy, DEL-ci).
20	
21	Index reference (C1): AAA=0, AA+=1, AA=2, AA-=3, A+=4, A=5, A-=6, BBB+=7, BBB=8, BBB-=9, BB+=10, BB=11, BB-=12, B+=13, B=14, B-=15, CCC+=16, CCC=17, CCC-=18.
22	
23	## Out of scope
24	
25	- Indicators 11, 12 and 13, and the rest of the REQ-06-02 notch calculator beyond this part (PRD-scope).
26	- Any UI, CLI, logging or printed output (C4, NFR-observability).
27	- Rating symbols outside the 19-step C1 scale, for example CC, C, D, NR, SD, or Moody's-style Baa1. They are rejected, not mapped (C2, CON-errors).
28	- Mapping between agency scales, outlooks or watch flags. Turning a notch count into a WL level.
29	- Storage, I/O, external integrations, configuration or feature flags (ARC-data, ARC-integration, DEL-deploy).
30	- npm dependencies, lint or typecheck tooling, and documentation or changelog updates (ARC-stack, DEL-ci, DEL-docs).
31	- A numeric coverage target (X-test-coverage).
32	
33	## Acceptance criteria
34	<!-- Each one must be testable. Cards reference these ids. -->
35	- **AC-1 (C1, Contract, X-scale-immutability):** Given `src/ratings/notch.mjs`, when `RATING_SCALE` is imported:
36	  - It deep-equals exactly `['AAA','AA+','AA','AA-','A+','A','A-','BBB+','BBB','BBB-','BB+','BB','BB-','B+','B','B-','CCC+','CCC','CCC-']`.
37	  - `RATING_SCALE.length === 19` and `Object.isFrozen(RATING_SCALE) === true`.
38	  - `RATING_SCALE.push('CC')` throws a `TypeError` (ESM strict mode), and afterwards `RATING_SCALE.length` is still `19`.
39	- **AC-2 (Contract, X-export-style):** Given the module, when it is imported with `import * as m from './src/ratings/notch.mjs'`:
40	  - `Object.keys(m).sort()` deep-equals `['RATING_SCALE','notchChange']`, so there is no default export.
41	  - `typeof m.notchChange === 'function'`.
42	- **AC-3 (REQ-06-02, C3):** Given previous `'BBB+'` and current `'BB+'`, when `notchChange('BBB+','BB+')` is called, then it returns `3` (a downgrade is positive).
43	- **AC-4 (REQ-06-02, C3):** Given previous `'BB+'` and current `'BBB+'`, when `notchChange('BB+','BBB+')` is called, then it returns `-3` (an upgrade is negative).
44	- **AC-5 (REQ-06-02, C3):** Given previous `'A'` and current `'A'`, when `notchChange('A','A')` is called, then it returns `0`. Also, for every `r` of `RATING_SCALE`, `notchChange(r, r) === 0`.
45	- **AC-6 (C1, C3, CON-interface):** Given any pair `(p, c)` from `RATING_SCALE` (all 361 pairs), when `notchChange(p, c)` is called:
46	  - It returns `RATING_SCALE.indexOf(c) - RATING_SCALE.indexOf(p)`.
47	  - `Number.isInteger(result)` is true.
48	  - `notchChange(c, p) === -notchChange(p, c)`, except that the `r→r` case is `0` (AC-5).
49	
50	  Spot values: `('AAA','AA+')` → `1`; `('A-','BBB+')` → `1`; `('BBB-','BB+')` → `1`; `('B-','CCC+')` → `1`; `('AA','A')` → `3`; `('CCC','B+')` → `-4`.
51	- **AC-7 (C3, CON-interface):** Given the two ends of the scale: `notchChange('AAA','CCC-')` returns `18`; `notchChange('CCC-','AAA')` returns `-18`; no pair returns a value outside `[-18, 18]`.
52	- **AC-8 (ARC-async):** Given valid inputs, when `notchChange('BBB','BB')` is called, then it returns the number `2` directly. `typeof result === 'number'`, and the result is not a Promise or a thenable.
53	- **AC-9 (C1, X-input-normalisation, case):** Given inputs that differ only in letter case: `notchChange('bbb+','bb+')` returns `3`; `notchChange('Aa-','aa-')` returns `0`; `notchChange('ccc-','aaa')` returns `-18`.
54	- **AC-10 (C1, X-input-normalisation, trim):** Given inputs with leading or trailing whitespace that `String.prototype.trim()` removes: `notchChange(' BBB+ ','\tBB+\n')` returns `3`; `notchChange(' A ','A')` returns `0`; `notchChange('﻿bb+ ', 'BBB+')` returns `-3`.
55	- **AC-11 (C1, C2, X-input-normalisation, inner whitespace):** Given a rating with whitespace inside it, when `notchChange('BBB +','A')` or `notchChange('A','B B')` is called, then a `RangeError` is thrown.
56	- **AC-12 (C2, CON-errors, unknown rating):** Given a string that is not one of the 19 ratings after trim and case-folding, then `notchChange(x,'A')` and `notchChange('A',x)` both throw a `RangeError`, for each `x` in `'CC'`, `'C'`, `'D'`, `'NR'`, `'SD'`, `'Baa1'`, `'AAA+'`, `'BBB++'`, `'A1'`, `'B--'`, `'CCC-+'`, `'AAAA'`, `'+'`, `'-'`.
57	- **AC-13 (C2, CON-errors, empty):** Given an empty or whitespace-only string, then a `RangeError` is thrown, for each `x` in `''`, `'   '`, `'\t\n'`, in either position.
58	- **AC-14 (C2, CON-errors, non-string):** Given a non-string argument, then a `RangeError` is thrown, not a `TypeError` and not any other error, for each `x` in `undefined`, `null`, `7`, `0`, `NaN`, `true`, `{}`, `['A']`, `new String('A')`, `Symbol('A')`, `() => 'A'`, `7n`, in either position. Also `notchChange('A')` (current missing) and `notchChange()` throw `RangeError`.
59	- **AC-15 (C2, X-error-message):** Given both arguments are invalid, for example `notchChange('XX', null)`, then a `RangeError` is thrown (no partial result, no fallback value). QA asserts only the error type. Per X-error-message, the message names `previous`, because `previous` is checked first.
60	- **AC-16 (C4, CLAUDE.md "pure functions, no I/O"):** Given the module, when it is imported and `notchChange` is called with valid and invalid inputs: nothing is written to stdout or stderr (`node -e "import('./src/ratings/notch.mjs').then(m=>{m.notchChange('A','B');try{m.notchChange('x','A')}catch{}})"` prints nothing and exits `0`); `src/ratings/notch.mjs` contains no `import` statement and no `console.` call; `RATING_SCALE` is unchanged after the calls.
61	- **AC-17 (Contract, CLAUDE.md, DEL-ci, TST-strategy):** Given the repo after the change: `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs` exists, uses `node:test` and `node:assert/strict`, and covers AC-1 to AC-16; `npm test` exits `0` with no failing tests; `package.json` declares no `dependencies` or `devDependencies`.
62	
63	## Risks and assumptions
64	
65	- **Risk: the developer runs on haiku.** Likely slips: throwing `TypeError` for non-strings instead of `RangeError` (AC-14); accepting `new String('A')` by using `String(x)` or `x.trim` duck-typing instead of `typeof x === 'string'` (AC-14); removing inner whitespace (AC-11); reversing the sign (AC-3/AC-4). The card spec states each explicitly. QA runs the full 361-pair check (AC-6).
66	- **Risk:** `Symbol('A')` breaks string conversion during error-message building (template literal → `TypeError`). The message must render the value safely so that the thrown error stays a `RangeError` (AC-14, X-error-message).
67	- **Assumption:** case-folding uses locale-independent `toUpperCase()` / `toLowerCase()`. Full-width characters such as `'ＡＡＡ'` are rejected (AC-12 behaviour).
68	- **Assumption:** extra arguments after the second are ignored. The request is silent, and this does not change scope.
69	- **Assumption:** `node --test` (no arguments) finds `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs`. CLAUDE.md requires Node 18+, so nothing may rely on newer features.
70	- **Resolved contradictions (PRD-conflicts):** the REQ-06-02 summary says "3-notch upgrade" with no sign; C3 settles it as `-3`. "next to the code under `test/`" means `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs`, per CLAUDE.md.

74	None. Readiness has 0 open items. The wording of the RangeError message is a PM decision (X-error-message) and does not change scope.

1	# Plan
2	
3	> Produced by the Business Analyst (MODE PLAN), written to this file by Michael. Keep the headings as they are — the ACs are checked one by one at closing.
4	
5	## Goal
6	
7	Provide one pure function that gives the signed notch change between a previous and a current credit rating. Indicators 11, 12 and 13 and the REQ-06-02 notch calculator are built on it (REQ-06-02 (part), readiness PRD-goal). Success means three things hold as automated tests in `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs`, and `npm test` passes:
8	- `notchChange('BBB+','BB+') === 3`
9	- `notchChange('BB+','BBB+') === -3`
10	- `notchChange('A','A') === 0`
11	
12	## Scope
13	
14	- A new module `src/ratings/notch.mjs` with exactly two named exports (Contract, X-export-style):
15	  - `RATING_SCALE`: a frozen array of the 19 C1 ratings, best first (C1, X-scale-immutability).
16	  - `notchChange(previous, current)`: synchronous. It returns the integer `index(current) - index(previous)` on `RATING_SCALE` (C3, CON-interface, ARC-async).
17	- Input normalisation: `String.prototype.trim()`, then a case-insensitive match. Inner whitespace is not removed (C1, X-input-normalisation).
18	- Every invalid argument, in either position, is rejected with a `RangeError` (C2, CON-errors). The message names the argument (`previous` / `current`) and the value received. `previous` is checked first (X-error-message).
19	- Unit tests with `node:test` and `node:assert/strict` in `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs`, run by `npm test` (CLAUDE.md, TST-strategy, DEL-ci).
20	
21	Index reference (C1): AAA=0, AA+=1, AA=2, AA-=3, A+=4, A=5, A-=6, BBB+=7, BBB=8, BBB-=9, BB+=10, BB=11, BB-=12, B+=13, B=14, B-=15, CCC+=16, CCC=17, CCC-=18.
22	
23	## Out of scope
24	
25	- Indicators 11, 12 and 13, and the rest of the REQ-06-02 notch calculator beyond this part (PRD-scope).
26	- Any UI, CLI, logging or printed output (C4, NFR-observability).
27	- Rating symbols outside the 19-step C1 scale, for example CC, C, D, NR, SD, or Moody's-style Baa1. They are rejected, not mapped (C2, CON-errors).
28	- Mapping between agency scales, outlooks or watch flags. Turning a notch count into a WL level.
29	- Storage, I/O, external integrations, configuration or feature flags (ARC-data, ARC-integration, DEL-deploy).
30	- npm dependencies, lint or typecheck tooling, and documentation or changelog updates (ARC-stack, DEL-ci, DEL-docs).
31	- A numeric coverage target (X-test-coverage).
32	
33	## Acceptance criteria
34	<!-- Each one must be testable. Cards reference these ids. -->
35	- **AC-1 (C1, Contract, X-scale-immutability):** Given `src/ratings/notch.mjs`, when `RATING_SCALE` is imported:
36	  - It deep-equals exactly `['AAA','AA+','AA','AA-','A+','A','A-','BBB+','BBB','BBB-','BB+','BB','BB-','B+','B','B-','CCC+','CCC','CCC-']`.
37	  - `RATING_SCALE.length === 19` and `Object.isFrozen(RATING_SCALE) === true`.
38	  - `RATING_SCALE.push('CC')` throws a `TypeError` (ESM strict mode), and afterwards `RATING_SCALE.length` is still `19`.
39	- **AC-2 (Contract, X-export-style):** Given the module, when it is imported with `import * as m from './src/ratings/notch.mjs'`:
40	  - `Object.keys(m).sort()` deep-equals `['RATING_SCALE','notchChange']`, so there is no default export.
41	  - `typeof m.notchChange === 'function'`.
42	- **AC-3 (REQ-06-02, C3):** Given previous `'BBB+'` and current `'BB+'`, when `notchChange('BBB+','BB+')` is called, then it returns `3` (a downgrade is positive).
43	- **AC-4 (REQ-06-02, C3):** Given previous `'BB+'` and current `'BBB+'`, when `notchChange('BB+','BBB+')` is called, then it returns `-3` (an upgrade is negative).
44	- **AC-5 (REQ-06-02, C3):** Given previous `'A'` and current `'A'`, when `notchChange('A','A')` is called, then it returns `0`. Also, for every `r` of `RATING_SCALE`, `notchChange(r, r) === 0`.
45	- **AC-6 (C1, C3, CON-interface):** Given any pair `(p, c)` from `RATING_SCALE` (all 361 pairs), when `notchChange(p, c)` is called:
46	  - It returns `RATING_SCALE.indexOf(c) - RATING_SCALE.indexOf(p)`.
47	  - `Number.isInteger(result)` is true.
48	  - `notchChange(c, p) === -notchChange(p, c)`, except that the `r→r` case is `0` (AC-5).
49	
50	  Spot values: `('AAA','AA+')` → `1`; `('A-','BBB+')` → `1`; `('BBB-','BB+')` → `1`; `('B-','CCC+')` → `1`; `('AA','A')` → `3`; `('CCC','B+')` → `-4`.
51	- **AC-7 (C3, CON-interface):** Given the two ends of the scale: `notchChange('AAA','CCC-')` returns `18`; `notchChange('CCC-','AAA')` returns `-18`; no pair returns a value outside `[-18, 18]`.
52	- **AC-8 (ARC-async):** Given valid inputs, when `notchChange('BBB','BB')` is called, then it returns the number `2` directly. `typeof result === 'number'`, and the result is not a Promise or a thenable.
53	- **AC-9 (C1, X-input-normalisation, case):** Given inputs that differ only in letter case: `notchChange('bbb+','bb+')` returns `3`; `notchChange('Aa-','aa-')` returns `0`; `notchChange('ccc-','aaa')` returns `-18`.
54	- **AC-10 (C1, X-input-normalisation, trim):** Given inputs with leading or trailing whitespace that `String.prototype.trim()` removes: `notchChange(' BBB+ ','\tBB+\n')` returns `3`; `notchChange(' A ','A')` returns `0`; `notchChange('﻿bb+ ', 'BBB+')` returns `-3`.
55	- **AC-11 (C1, C2, X-input-normalisation, inner whitespace):** Given a rating with whitespace inside it, when `notchChange('BBB +','A')` or `notchChange('A','B B')` is called, then a `RangeError` is thrown.
56	- **AC-12 (C2, CON-errors, unknown rating):** Given a string that is not one of the 19 ratings after trim and case-folding, then `notchChange(x,'A')` and `notchChange('A',x)` both throw a `RangeError`, for each `x` in `'CC'`, `'C'`, `'D'`, `'NR'`, `'SD'`, `'Baa1'`, `'AAA+'`, `'BBB++'`, `'A1'`, `'B--'`, `'CCC-+'`, `'AAAA'`, `'+'`, `'-'`.
57	- **AC-13 (C2, CON-errors, empty):** Given an empty or whitespace-only string, then a `RangeError` is thrown, for each `x` in `''`, `'   '`, `'\t\n'`, in either position.
58	- **AC-14 (C2, CON-errors, non-string):** Given a non-string argument, then a `RangeError` is thrown, not a `TypeError` and not any other error, for each `x` in `undefined`, `null`, `7`, `0`, `NaN`, `true`, `{}`, `['A']`, `new String('A')`, `Symbol('A')`, `() => 'A'`, `7n`, in either position. Also `notchChange('A')` (current missing) and `notchChange()` throw `RangeError`.
59	- **AC-15 (C2, X-error-message):** Given both arguments are invalid, for example `notchChange('XX', null)`, then a `RangeError` is thrown (no partial result, no fallback value). QA asserts only the error type. Per X-error-message, the message names `previous`, because `previous` is checked first.
60	- **AC-16 (C4, CLAUDE.md "pure functions, no I/O"):** Given the module, when it is imported and `notchChange` is called with valid and invalid inputs: nothing is written to stdout or stderr (`node -e "import('./src/ratings/notch.mjs').then(m=>{m.notchChange('A','B');try{m.notchChange('x','A')}catch{}})"` prints nothing and exits `0`); `src/ratings/notch.mjs` contains no `import` statement and no `console.` call; `RATING_SCALE` is unchanged after the calls.
61	- **AC-17 (Contract, CLAUDE.md, DEL-ci, TST-strategy):** Given the repo after the change: `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs` exists, uses `node:test` and `node:assert/strict`, and covers AC-1 to AC-16; `npm test` exits `0` with no failing tests; `package.json` declares no `dependencies` or `devDependencies`.
62

=== T-01 ===
# T-01: ratings-lib: add src/ratings/notch.mjs (RATING_SCALE + notchChange) with unit tests

## User story
As the developer of Indicators 11, 12 and 13 and the REQ-06-02 notch calculator, I want one pure, synchronous function that gives the signed notch change between a previous and a current credit rating, so that every indicator counts downgrades and upgrades the same way, on one fixed scale.

## Traces to
AC-1 to AC-17 of plan.md. REQ-06-02 (part). Readiness decisions: C1, C2, C3, C4, Contract, CON-interface, CON-errors, ARC-async, X-export-style, X-scale-immutability, X-input-normalisation, X-error-message, TST-strategy, DEL-ci, and CLAUDE.md.

## What to build
- `src/ratings/notch.mjs` (new) has exactly two named exports.
  - `RATING_SCALE`: a frozen array of the 19 ratings, best first.
  - `notchChange(previous, current)`: synchronous. It returns `index(current) - index(previous)`.
- `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs` (new) tests it with `node:test` and `node:assert/strict`.
- No other files change. `package.json` is not edited.

Index reference: AAA=0, AA+=1, AA=2, AA-=3, A+=4, A=5, A-=6, BBB+=7, BBB=8, BBB-=9, BB+=10, BB=11, BB-=12, B+=13, B=14, B-=15, CCC+=16, CCC=17, CCC-=18.

## Acceptance criteria
Dev checks these with unit tests in `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs`. QA checks them through the public import `../../../src/ratings/notch.mjs` from `test/integration/ratings/*.test.mjs`. Error checks use `assert.throws(fn, RangeError)`.

1. (AC-1) Given the module, when `RATING_SCALE` is imported, then:
   - it deep-equals `['AAA','AA+','AA','AA-','A+','A','A-','BBB+','BBB','BBB-','BB+','BB','BB-','B+','B','B-','CCC+','CCC','CCC-']`;
   - `RATING_SCALE.length === 19` and `Object.isFrozen(RATING_SCALE) === true`;
   - `RATING_SCALE.push('CC')` throws `TypeError`, and the length is still `19` afterwards.
2. (AC-2) Given `import * as m from '…/src/ratings/notch.mjs'`, then `Object.keys(m).sort()` deep-equals `['RATING_SCALE','notchChange']`, `m.default === undefined`, and `typeof m.notchChange === 'function'`.
3. (AC-3) Given `('BBB+','BB+')`, when `notchChange` is called, then it returns `3` (a downgrade is positive).
4. (AC-4) Given `('BB+','BBB+')`, when `notchChange` is called, then it returns `-3` (an upgrade is negative).
5. (AC-5) Given `('A','A')`, when `notchChange` is called, then it returns `0`, and `notchChange(r, r) === 0` for each of the 19 `r` in `RATING_SCALE`.
6. (AC-6) Given all 361 pairs `(p, c)` from `RATING_SCALE`, when `notchChange(p, c)` is called, then:
   - the result `=== RATING_SCALE.indexOf(c) - RATING_SCALE.indexOf(p)`;
   - `Number.isInteger(result)` is true;
   - `notchChange(c, p) === -notchChange(p, c)`, comparing `0` with `===`, not `Object.is`, so that `-0` is not an issue.
   - Spot values: `('AAA','AA+')`→`1`, `('A-','BBB+')`→`1`, `('BBB-','BB+')`→`1`, `('B-','CCC+')`→`1`, `('AA','A')`→`3`, `('CCC','B+')`→`-4`.
7. (AC-7) Given the two ends of the scale, then `notchChange('AAA','CCC-') === 18`, `notchChange('CCC-','AAA') === -18`, and every one of the 361 results lies in `[-18, 18]`.
8. (AC-8) Given `('BBB','BB')`, when `notchChange` is called, then it returns `2` directly: `typeof result === 'number'`, `result instanceof Promise` is false, and `typeof result.then === 'undefined'`.
9. (AC-9) Given inputs that differ only in case, then:
   - `notchChange('bbb+','bb+') === 3`;
   - `notchChange('Aa-','aa-') === 0`;
   - `notchChange('ccc-','aaa') === -18`.
10. (AC-10) Given leading or trailing whitespace that `String.prototype.trim()` removes, then:
    - `notchChange(' BBB+ ','\tBB+\n') === 3`;
    - `notchChange(' A ','A') === 0`;
    - `notchChange('\uFEFFbb+ ','BBB+') === -3`, because the BOM is trimmed.
11. (AC-11) Given whitespace inside a rating, then `notchChange('BBB +','A')` and `notchChange('A','B B')` each throw `RangeError`. Inner whitespace is never removed.
12. (AC-12) Given an unknown symbol `x` from the list below, then `notchChange(x,'A')` and `notchChange('A',x)` each throw `RangeError` (28 assertions):
    - `'CC'`, `'C'`, `'D'`, `'NR'`, `'SD'`, `'Baa1'`, `'AAA+'`, `'BBB++'`, `'A1'`, `'B--'`, `'CCC-+'`, `'AAAA'`, `'+'`, `'-'`.
    - The full-width `'ＡＡＡ'` is also rejected in both positions.
13. (AC-13) Given an empty or whitespace-only string `x` in `''`, `'   '`, `'\t\n'`, then `notchChange(x,'A')` and `notchChange('A',x)` each throw `RangeError`.
14. (AC-14) Given a non-string `x` from the list below, then `notchChange(x,'A')` and `notchChange('A',x)` each throw `RangeError`. A `TypeError` fails this criterion: assert `err instanceof RangeError` and `err.constructor === RangeError`.
    - `undefined`, `null`, `7`, `0`, `NaN`, `true`, `{}`, `['A']`, `new String('A')`, `Symbol('A')`, `() => 'A'`, `7n`, `Object.create(null)`.
    - `notchChange('A')` and `notchChange()` each throw `RangeError`.
15. (AC-15) Given both arguments are invalid, then `notchChange('XX', null)` throws `RangeError` with no return value. Dev also asserts that `err.message` contains `'previous'` and not `'current'`. QA asserts only the type.
    - (AC-15, X-error-message) For a single bad argument, the message names it and shows the received value. For example, `notchChange('A', null)` gives a message that contains `'current'` and `'null'`, and `notchChange('XX','A')` gives a message that contains `'previous'` and `'XX'`.
16. (AC-16) Given the module, then:
    - from the repo root, `node -e "import('./src/ratings/notch.mjs').then(m=>{m.notchChange('A','B');try{m.notchChange('x','A')}catch{}})"` prints nothing to stdout or stderr and exits `0`;
    - the source matches neither `/^\s*import\s/m` nor `/console\./` (the test may read it with `node:fs`);
    - after all the calls above, `RATING_SCALE` still deep-equals the AC-1 array.
17. (AC-17) Given the repo after the change, then:
    - `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs` exists, imports `node:test` and `node:assert/strict`, and covers criteria 1 to 16;
    - `node --test test/ratings/notch.test.mjs` and `npm test` both exit `0` with 0 failing tests;
    - `package.json` has no `dependencies` or `devDependencies` and is unchanged;
    - the commits are titled `T-01: …` and have no AI attribution.

## Edge cases
- **Validation order:** `previous` is validated completely (type, trim, match) before `current` is looked at. Extra arguments are ignored: `notchChange('A','B','junk') === 9`.
- **Type check:** only `typeof x === 'string'` counts as a string. String objects, arrays such as `['A']`, and functions are rejected, even when they would turn into a valid rating.
- **Safe error message:** building the message must not throw for any value. A template literal on `Symbol('A')` or `Object.create(null)` throws `TypeError`, and so does `JSON.stringify(7n)`. The thrown error must still be a `RangeError` for these values.
- **Case-folding:** use `toUpperCase()`, which does not depend on locale. Do not use `toLocaleUpperCase` and do not apply Unicode normalisation.
- **Result:** for valid input the result is always an integer in `[-18, 18]`, never `NaN` and never a non-integer, and the module has no fallback value.
- **Purity:** calls never mutate `RATING_SCALE`, and repeated calls give identical results.
- **Node version:** nothing newer than Node 18 may be used, for example `toSorted` or `Object.groupBy`. The test file must be found by bare `node --test`.

## Test data
| previous | current | expected |
|---|---|---|
| `'BBB+'` | `'BB+'` | `3` |
| `'BB+'` | `'BBB+'` | `-3` |
| `'A'` | `'A'` | `0` |
| `'AAA'` | `'CCC-'` | `18` |
| `'CCC-'` | `'AAA'` | `-18` |
| `'AA'` | `'A'` | `3` |
| `'CCC'` | `'B+'` | `-4` |
| `'A-'` | `'BBB+'` | `1` |
| `'BBB'` | `'BB'` | `2` (a number, not a Promise) |
| `'bbb+'` | `'bb+'` | `3` |
| `'Aa-'` | `'aa-'` | `0` |
| `' BBB+ '` | `'\tBB+\n'` | `3` |
| `'\uFEFFbb+ '` | `'BBB+'` | `-3` |
| `'BBB +'` | `'A'` | RangeError |
| `'A'` | `'B B'` | RangeError |
| `'CC'` / `'NR'` / `'Baa1'` / `'AAA+'` / `'ＡＡＡ'` | `'A'` | RangeError |
| `'A'` | `''` / `'   '` / `'\t\n'` | RangeError |
| `null` / `undefined` / `7` / `NaN` / `true` / `{}` | `'A'` | RangeError |
| `new String('A')` / `['A']` / `() => 'A'` | `'A'` | RangeError |
| `Symbol('A')` / `7n` / `Object.create(null)` | `'A'` | RangeError, not TypeError |
| `'A'` | (missing) | RangeError |
| (missing) | (missing) | RangeError |
| `'XX'` | `null` | RangeError, and the message names `previous` |

## Out of scope for this card
- Indicators 11, 12 and 13, the rest of the REQ-06-02 calculator, and turning a notch count into a WL level.
- Mapping between agency scales (Moody's), outlooks and watch flags.
- Ratings below CCC-: CC, C, D, NR and SD are rejected, not mapped.
- CLI, UI, logging, storage, config and feature flags.
- npm dependencies, lint and typecheck tooling, docs and changelog, and a numeric coverage target.
- Any file other than `src/ratings/notch.mjs` and `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs`.
- QA's integration tests go in `test/integration/ratings/` (QA's scope, not the dev's). Because `npm test` runs every test file, they run there too and must pass.

---

Notes for Michael:

- **I changed nothing in the plan.** I added four test points for things the plan's rules already require:
  - `Object.create(null)` in criterion 14, which the card's `describe()` helper already handles;
  - full-width `'ＡＡＡ'` in criterion 12, from the plan's assumptions;
  - the extra-argument example in Edge cases;
  - the message-content example in criterion 15.
- **Node version:** this machine runs Node v22.22.0, but the project requires Node 18+. A green `npm test` here does not prove the code runs on Node 18, so the "nothing newer than Node 18" rule needs to be checked in code review.
- **Checked in Node 22:** `trim()` removes U+FEFF, `push` on the frozen array throws `TypeError`, a template literal on `Object.create(null)` throws `TypeError`, and `'ＡＡＡ'.toUpperCase()` is not `'AAA'`.

# T-01: ratings-lib: add src/ratings/notch.mjs (RATING_SCALE + notchChange) with unit tests

## User story
As the developer of Indicators 11, 12 and 13 and the REQ-06-02 notch calculator, I want one pure, synchronous function that gives the signed notch change between a previous and a current credit rating, so that every indicator counts downgrades and upgrades the same way, on one fixed scale.

## Traces to
AC-1 to AC-17 of plan.md. REQ-06-02 (part). Readiness decisions: C1, C2, C3, C4, Contract, CON-interface, CON-errors, ARC-async, X-export-style, X-scale-immutability, X-input-normalisation, X-error-message, TST-strategy, DEL-ci, and CLAUDE.md.

## What to build
- `src/ratings/notch.mjs` (new) has exactly two named exports.
  - `RATING_SCALE`: a frozen array of the 19 ratings, best first.
  - `notchChange(previous, current)`: synchronous. It returns `index(current) - index(previous)`.
- `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs` (new) tests it with `node:test` and `node:assert/strict`.
- No other files change. `package.json` is not edited.

Index reference: AAA=0, AA+=1, AA=2, AA-=3, A+=4, A=5, A-=6, BBB+=7, BBB=8, BBB-=9, BB+=10, BB=11, BB-=12, B+=13, B=14, B-=15, CCC+=16, CCC=17, CCC-=18.

## Acceptance criteria
Dev checks these with unit tests in `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs`. QA checks them through the public import `../../../src/ratings/notch.mjs` from `test/integration/ratings/*.test.mjs`. Error checks use `assert.throws(fn, RangeError)`.

1. (AC-1) Given the module, when `RATING_SCALE` is imported, then:
   - it deep-equals `['AAA','AA+','AA','AA-','A+','A','A-','BBB+','BBB','BBB-','BB+','BB','BB-','B+','B','B-','CCC+','CCC','CCC-']`;
   - `RATING_SCALE.length === 19` and `Object.isFrozen(RATING_SCALE) === true`;
   - `RATING_SCALE.push('CC')` throws `TypeError`, and the length is still `19` afterwards.
2. (AC-2) Given `import * as m from '…/src/ratings/notch.mjs'`, then `Object.keys(m).sort()` deep-equals `['RATING_SCALE','notchChange']`, `m.default === undefined`, and `typeof m.notchChange === 'function'`.
3. (AC-3) Given `('BBB+','BB+')`, when `notchChange` is called, then it returns `3` (a downgrade is positive).
4. (AC-4) Given `('BB+','BBB+')`, when `notchChange` is called, then it returns `-3` (an upgrade is negative).
5. (AC-5) Given `('A','A')`, when `notchChange` is called, then it returns `0`, and `notchChange(r, r) === 0` for each of the 19 `r` in `RATING_SCALE`.
6. (AC-6) Given all 361 pairs `(p, c)` from `RATING_SCALE`, when `notchChange(p, c)` is called, then the result `=== RATING_SCALE.indexOf(c) - RATING_SCALE.indexOf(p)`; `Number.isInteger(result)` is true; `notchChange(c, p) === -notchChange(p, c)` (compare `0` with `===`, so `-0` is not an issue). Spot values: `('AAA','AA+')`→`1`, `('A-','BBB+')`→`1`, `('BBB-','BB+')`→`1`, `('B-','CCC+')`→`1`, `('AA','A')`→`3`, `('CCC','B+')`→`-4`.
7. (AC-7) Given the two ends of the scale, then `notchChange('AAA','CCC-') === 18`, `notchChange('CCC-','AAA') === -18`, and every one of the 361 results lies in `[-18, 18]`.
8. (AC-8) Given `('BBB','BB')`, when `notchChange` is called, then it returns `2` directly: `typeof result === 'number'`, `result instanceof Promise` is false, and `typeof result.then === 'undefined'`.
9. (AC-9) Given inputs that differ only in case, then `notchChange('bbb+','bb+') === 3`; `notchChange('Aa-','aa-') === 0`; `notchChange('ccc-','aaa') === -18`.
10. (AC-10) Given leading or trailing whitespace that `String.prototype.trim()` removes, then `notchChange(' BBB+ ','\tBB+\n') === 3`; `notchChange(' A ','A') === 0` (no-break space); `notchChange('﻿bb+ ','BBB+') === -3`, because the BOM is trimmed.
11. (AC-11) Given whitespace inside a rating, then `notchChange('BBB +','A')` and `notchChange('A','B B')` each throw `RangeError`. Inner whitespace is never removed.
12. (AC-12) Given an unknown symbol `x` in `'CC'`, `'C'`, `'D'`, `'NR'`, `'SD'`, `'Baa1'`, `'AAA+'`, `'BBB++'`, `'A1'`, `'B--'`, `'CCC-+'`, `'AAAA'`, `'+'`, `'-'`, then `notchChange(x,'A')` and `notchChange('A',x)` each throw `RangeError`. The full-width `'ＡＡＡ'` is also rejected in both positions.
13. (AC-13) Given an empty or whitespace-only string `x` in `''`, `'   '`, `'\t\n'`, then `notchChange(x,'A')` and `notchChange('A',x)` each throw `RangeError`.
14. (AC-14) Given a non-string `x` in `undefined`, `null`, `7`, `0`, `NaN`, `true`, `{}`, `['A']`, `new String('A')`, `Symbol('A')`, `() => 'A'`, `7n`, `Object.create(null)`, then `notchChange(x,'A')` and `notchChange('A',x)` each throw `RangeError`. A `TypeError` fails this criterion: assert `err instanceof RangeError` and `err.constructor === RangeError`. Also `notchChange('A')` and `notchChange()` each throw `RangeError`.
15. (AC-15) Given both arguments are invalid, then `notchChange('XX', null)` throws `RangeError` with no return value. Dev also asserts that `err.message` contains `'previous'` and not `'current'`. QA asserts only the type. For a single bad argument, the message names it and shows the received value: `notchChange('A', null)` gives a message containing `'current'` and `'null'`; `notchChange('XX','A')` gives a message containing `'previous'` and `'XX'`.
16. (AC-16) Given the module, then: from the repo root, `node -e "import('./src/ratings/notch.mjs').then(m=>{m.notchChange('A','B');try{m.notchChange('x','A')}catch{}})"` prints nothing to stdout or stderr and exits `0`; the source matches neither `/^\s*import\s/m` nor `/console\./` (the test may read it with `node:fs`); after all the calls above, `RATING_SCALE` still deep-equals the AC-1 array.
17. (AC-17) Given the repo after the change, then: `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs` exists, imports `node:test` and `node:assert/strict`, and covers criteria 1 to 16; `node --test test/ratings/notch.test.mjs` and `npm test` both exit `0` with 0 failing tests; `package.json` has no `dependencies` or `devDependencies` and is unchanged; the commits are titled `T-01: …` and have no AI attribution.

## Edge cases
- **Validation order:** `previous` is validated completely (type, trim, match) before `current` is looked at. Extra arguments are ignored: `notchChange('A','B','junk') === 1`.
- **Type check:** only `typeof x === 'string'` counts as a string. String objects, arrays such as `['A']`, and functions are rejected, even when they would turn into a valid rating.
- **Safe error message:** building the message must not throw for any value. A template literal on `Symbol('A')` or `Object.create(null)` throws `TypeError`, and so does `JSON.stringify(7n)`. The thrown error must still be a `RangeError` for these values.
- **Case-folding:** use `toUpperCase()`, which does not depend on locale. Do not use `toLocaleUpperCase` and do not apply Unicode normalisation.
- **Result:** for valid input the result is always an integer in `[-18, 18]`, never `NaN`, and the module has no fallback value.
- **Purity:** calls never mutate `RATING_SCALE`, and repeated calls give identical results.
- **Node version:** nothing newer than Node 18 may be used, for example `toSorted` or `Object.groupBy`. The test file must be found by bare `node --test`.

2	
3	## User story
4	As the developer of Indicators 11, 12 and 13 and the REQ-06-02 notch calculator, I want one pure, synchronous function that gives the signed notch change between a previous and a current credit rating, so that every indicator counts downgrades and upgrades the same way, on one fixed scale.
5	
6	## Traces to
7	AC-1 to AC-17 of plan.md. REQ-06-02 (part). Readiness decisions: C1, C2, C3, C4, Contract, CON-interface, CON-errors, ARC-async, X-export-style, X-scale-immutability, X-input-normalisation, X-error-message, TST-strategy, DEL-ci, and CLAUDE.md.
8	
9	## What to build
10	- `src/ratings/notch.mjs` (new) has exactly two named exports.
11	  - `RATING_SCALE`: a frozen array of the 19 ratings, best first.
12	  - `notchChange(previous, current)`: synchronous. It returns `index(current) - index(previous)`.
13	- `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs` (new) tests it with `node:test` and `node:assert/strict`.
14	- No other files change. `package.json` is not edited.
15	
16	Index reference: AAA=0, AA+=1, AA=2, AA-=3, A+=4, A=5, A-=6, BBB+=7, BBB=8, BBB-=9, BB+=10, BB=11, BB-=12, B+=13, B=14, B-=15, CCC+=16, CCC=17, CCC-=18.
17	
18	## Acceptance criteria
19	Dev checks these with unit tests in `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs`. QA checks them through the public import `../../../src/ratings/notch.mjs` from `test/ratings/integration/*.test.mjs`. Error checks use `assert.throws(fn, RangeError)`.
20	
21	1. (AC-1) Given the module, when `RATING_SCALE` is imported, then:
22	   - it deep-equals `['AAA','AA+','AA','AA-','A+','A','A-','BBB+','BBB','BBB-','BB+','BB','BB-','B+','B','B-','CCC+','CCC','CCC-']`;
23	   - `RATING_SCALE.length === 19` and `Object.isFrozen(RATING_SCALE) === true`;
24	   - `RATING_SCALE.push('CC')` throws `TypeError`, and the length is still `19` afterwards.
25	2. (AC-2) Given `import * as m from '…/src/ratings/notch.mjs'`, then `Object.keys(m).sort()` deep-equals `['RATING_SCALE','notchChange']`, `m.default === undefined`, and `typeof m.notchChange === 'function'`.
26	3. (AC-3) Given `('BBB+','BB+')`, when `notchChange` is called, then it returns `3` (a downgrade is positive).
27	4. (AC-4) Given `('BB+','BBB+')`, when `notchChange` is called, then it returns `-3` (an upgrade is negative).
28	5. (AC-5) Given `('A','A')`, when `notchChange` is called, then it returns `0`, and `notchChange(r, r) === 0` for each of the 19 `r` in `RATING_SCALE`.
29	6. (AC-6) Given all 361 pairs `(p, c)` from `RATING_SCALE`, when `notchChange(p, c)` is called, then the result `=== RATING_SCALE.indexOf(c) - RATING_SCALE.indexOf(p)`; `Number.isInteger(result)` is true; `notchChange(c, p) === -notchChange(p, c)` (compare `0` with `===`, so `-0` is not an issue). Spot values: `('AAA','AA+')`→`1`, `('A-','BBB+')`→`1`, `('BBB-','BB+')`→`1`, `('B-','CCC+')`→`1`, `('AA','A')`→`3`, `('CCC','B+')`→`-4`.
30	7. (AC-7) Given the two ends of the scale, then `notchChange('AAA','CCC-') === 18`, `notchChange('CCC-','AAA') === -18`, and every one of the 361 results lies in `[-18, 18]`.
31	8. (AC-8) Given `('BBB','BB')`, when `notchChange` is called, then it returns `2` directly: `typeof result === 'number'`, `result instanceof Promise` is false, and `typeof result.then === 'undefined'`.
32	9. (AC-9) Given inputs that differ only in case, then `notchChange('bbb+','bb+') === 3`; `notchChange('Aa-','aa-') === 0`; `notchChange('ccc-','aaa') === -18`.
33	10. (AC-10) Given leading or trailing whitespace that `String.prototype.trim()` removes, then `notchChange(' BBB+ ','\tBB+\n') === 3`; `notchChange(' A ','A') === 0` (no-break space); `notchChange('﻿bb+ ','BBB+') === -3`, because the BOM is trimmed.
34	11. (AC-11) Given whitespace inside a rating, then `notchChange('BBB +','A')` and `notchChange('A','B B')` each throw `RangeError`. Inner whitespace is never removed.
35	12. 37	14. A `TypeError` fails this criterion: assert `err instanceof RangeError` and `err.constructor === RangeError`. Also `notchChange('A')` and `notchChange()` each throw `RangeError`.

Dev also asserts that `err.message` contains `'previous'` and not `'current'`. QA asserts only the type. (AC-16) Given the module, then: from the repo root, `node -e "import('./src/ratings/notch.mjs').then(m=>{m.notchChange('A','B');try{m.notchChange('x','A')}catch{}})"` prints nothing to stdout or stderr and exits `0`; the source matches neither `/^\s*import\s/m` nor `/console\./` (the test may read it with `node:fs`); after all the calls above, `RATING_SCALE` still deep-equals the AC-1 array.

(AC-17) Given the repo after the change, then: `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs` exists, imports `node:test` and `node:assert/strict`, and covers criteria 1 to 16; `node --test test/ratings/notch.test.mjs` and `npm test` both exit `0` with 0 failing tests; `package.json` has no `dependencies` or `devDependencies` and is unchanged; the commits are titled `T-01: …` and have no AI attribution.

43	- **Validation order:** `previous` is validated completely (type, trim, match) before `current` is looked at. Extra arguments are ignored: `notchChange('A','B','junk') === 9`.
44	- **Type check:** only `typeof x === 'string'` counts as a string. String objects, arrays such as `['A']`, and functions are rejected, even when they would turn into a valid rating.

12	## Scope
13	
14	- A new module `src/ratings/notch.mjs` with exactly two named exports (Contract, X-export-style):
15	  - `RATING_SCALE`: a frozen array of the 19 C1 ratings, best first (C1, X-scale-immutability).

+// Pure function: no imports, no I/O, no side effects
+
+const RATING_SCALE = Object.freeze([
+  'AAA', 'AA+', 'AA', 'AA-', 'A+', 'A', 'A-',
+  'BBB+', 'BBB', 'BBB-', 'BB+', 'BB', 'BB-',
+  'B+', 'B', 'B-', 'CCC+', 'CCC', 'CCC-'
+])
+
+// Build a case-insensitive lookup map for fast matching
+const ratingLookup = new Map()
+for (const rating of RATING_SCALE) {
+  ratingLookup.set(rating.toUpperCase(), rating)
+}
+
+// Helper function to safely describe a value in an error message
+function describe(value) {
+  const t = typeof value
+  if (t === 'string') {
+    return JSON.stringify(value)
+  }
+  if (t === 'symbol') {
+    return String(value)
+  }
+  if (t === 'bigint') {
+    return String(value) + 'n'
+  }
+  if (t === 'function') {
+    return 'function'
+  }
+  if (value === null) {
+    return 'null'
+  }
+  if (t === 'object') {
+    if (Array.isArray(value)) {
+      return 'array'
+    }
+    return 'object'
+  }
+  return String(value)
+}
+
+// Helper function to validate and normalize a single rating argument
+function validateRating(value, argName) {
+  // Step (a): type check - only primitive strings
+  if (typeof value !== 'string') {
+    throw new RangeError(`Invalid ${argName} rating: received ${describe(value)}`)
+  }
+
+  // Step (b): trim
+  const trimmed = value.trim()
+
+  // Step (c) and (d): case-insensitive match
+  const upper = trimmed.toUpperCase()
+  if (!ratingLookup.has(upper)) {
+    throw new RangeError(`Invalid ${argName} rating: received ${JSON.stringify(value)}`)
+  }
+
+  // Return the canonical rating from the scale
+  return ratingLookup.get(upper)
+}
+
+// Main function: returns signed notch change
+function notchChange(previous, current) {
+  // Validate previous first
+  const prevRating = validateRating(previous, 'previous')
+
+  // Then validate current
+  const currRating = validateRating(current, 'current')
+
+  // Calculate the difference
+  const prevIndex = RATING_SCALE.indexOf(prevRating)
+  const currIndex = RATING_SCALE.indexOf(currRating)
+
+  // Convert -0 to 0 by explicitly checking and normalizing
+  const diff = currIndex - prevIndex
+  return diff === 0 ? 0 : diff
+}
+
+export { RATING_SCALE, notchChange }
